<compartment start="15" end="22" title="Stopped contrastive loss cliff" episode_type="investigation,bug" importance="82">
<p1>
U: "can you chase the loss cliff, not tune around it"

Investigated Nereid's contrastive trainer after loss jumped from 0.42 to 3.8 around step 17.8k on A100 runs. The tempting path was LR tuning, but crop-hash logging showed duplicated augmentations across dataloader workers after worker_init_fn was dropped in 6fb2d90. Restored per-worker seeding in training/data/seed.py, added epoch_seed to the run manifest, and reran runs/2026-05-08/a100-bf16-rerun through 52k steps without the cliff. Commit c8e4a11.
</p1>
<p2>
Nereid's loss cliff was caused by shared augmentation seeds across dataloader workers, not optimizer settings. training/data/seed.py now derives worker seeds from base seed, worker id, and epoch.
</p2>
<p3>
Nereid contrastive training stabilized after restoring per-worker augmentation seeds.
</p3>
<p4>worker_init_fn; augmentation_seed; runs/2026-05-08/a100-bf16-rerun</p4>
</compartment>
<facts>
<CONSTRAINTS>
* Nereid's contrastive trainer can diverge if augmentation_seed is shared across dataloader workers.
</CONSTRAINTS>
<CONFIG_VALUES>
* Nereid worker augmentation seed formula is base_seed + worker_id + epoch * 1009.
</CONFIG_VALUES>
</facts>
<events>
<causal_incident at_compartment="2">
  <summary>Training loss cliff traced to duplicated augmentation seeds.</summary>
  <affected_surface>other</affected_surface>
  <symptom>Contrastive loss jumped from 0.42 to 3.8 around step 17.8k on A100 runs.</symptom>
  <cause_summary>worker_init_fn had been removed, causing dataloader workers to reuse augmentation seeds.</cause_summary>
  <disposition>fixed</disposition>
  <evidence>Crop-hash logging showed duplicated augmentations across dataloader workers.</evidence>
  <fix_summary>Restored per-worker seed derivation in training/data/seed.py and recorded epoch_seed in run manifests.</fix_summary>
</causal_incident>
</events>

<compartment start="160" end="168" title="Manual page rotation escape hatch" episode_type="feature,bug" importance="27">
<p1>
Started by trying to auto-rotate ugly multi-scan uploads in the docket OCR intake, then backed away from making low-confidence guesses.
U: if confidence is fuzzy, give support a knob instead of guessing.

ingest/api/src/routes/upload.ts now stores an optional per-page rotation override alongside the upload manifest, and web/src/components/PageRotationOverride.tsx gives support a manual control in triage. Automatic rotation only applies when the OCR angle model is confidently right; the rest stay untouched until a human steps in. docs/support/scan-triage.md covers when to use the override. Commit 7ab2c54.
</p1>
<p2>
The rotation fix became a support-side escape hatch, not aggressive automation.
U: if confidence is fuzzy, give support a knob instead of guessing.

ingest/api/src/routes/upload.ts persists per-page overrides, web/src/components/PageRotationOverride.tsx exposes them in triage, and auto-rotation stays gated behind a high confidence threshold.
</p2>
<p3>
Low-confidence scan rotation is now handled through a manual override path, with automation reserved for only the most certain OCR angle predictions.
</p3>
<p4>PageRotationOverride; upload manifest override; angle_confidence threshold</p4>
</compartment>
<facts>
<CONSTRAINTS>
* OCR angle predictions below a high confidence threshold are not reliable enough for unattended page rotation on messy multi-scan uploads.
</CONSTRAINTS>
<CONFIG_VALUES>
* Automatic rotation threshold: angle_confidence 0.98 or higher.
</CONFIG_VALUES>
</facts>
<events>
<trajectory_correction at_compartment="19">
  <summary>Changed scan rotation from auto-fix ambition to manual override with high-confidence automation only.</summary>
  <before_strategy>Use OCR angle predictions to auto-rotate problematic scans broadly during ingest.</before_strategy>
  <correction_source>user</correction_source>
  <correction_signal>U: if confidence is fuzzy, give support a knob instead of guessing.</correction_signal>
  <after_strategy>Persist per-page rotation overrides and reserve automatic rotation for only high-confidence predictions.</after_strategy>
  <evidence>The final implementation added PageRotationOverride in triage UI and left ingest auto-rotation behind a strict confidence gate.</evidence>
</trajectory_correction>
</events>
<user_observations>
* User accepts deterministic manual escape hatches faster than vague low-confidence automation when support burden is obvious.

<compartment start="34" end="48" title="Java M3 follow-up fixes + Python D handlers (analyze/enroll/plan) delivered" episode_type="feature,bug" importance="70">
<p1>
While the Java follow-up round was being prepared, the Python lane returned its first delivery: the three D worker handlers `assessment.analyze`, `identity.enroll`, `plan.generate` under `backend/worker-python/src/mvp_worker/handlers/`, backed by a new `handlers/dshared/` package — `constants.py` (FIXED_NS f988d041-…, deterministic uuid5 helpers), `dconfig.py`, `providers.py` (FacePort/SkinPort/PlanPort protocols + deterministic `FaceDouble`/`SkinDouble`/`PlanDouble` with fault injection, and `AliyunFaceAdapter`/`AliyunSkinAdapter`/`AliyunPlanAdapter` that raise `ProviderNotActivated`), `jsonschema_support.py` (draft 2020-12 with common.json `$ref` inlining), `denqueue.py` (T12 helpers + `EnrollSlotOccupied` from `uq_job_identity_enroll`), `dmedia.py` (pending→put→available archival) and `resolve.py` (production fail-closed → retryable `DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE`). Handler `__init__.py` appended D registrations only; `test_unsupported.py` and `test_sanity.py` were adjusted. 86 tests green. Two decisions I flagged then: `identity.enroll` uses a namespace-level owner UUID `uuid5(FIXED_NS, "identity-namespace:{ns}")` so the partial unique index serializes the whole namespace, and `plan.generate` used a wait-hop that bumped `care_plans.generation_revision` and enqueued a successor at `now + MVP_PLAN_WAIT_CHECK_SECONDS` (default 30) — both later reversed by 总协调.

The Java follow-up round closed two review items: `AssessmentAcceptanceService` now enforces that the merged view map key set is exactly `{front,left,right}` with no nulls (else INTERNAL thrown inside the business tx, rolling the whole acceptance back, so `PhotoVersions.append` can never append a partial view set), and `SkinReportService` gained `validateStructure(report_payload)` so a present `conclusion`/`description` must be textual and `metrics`/`images` arrays — malformed payloads become 500 INTERNAL with no raw echo. Tests grew to 175. One deviation: the requested A05 malformed-payload seed was impossible under the V1 check constraints (`ck_assessment_report_payload_schema` requires a jsonb object with numeric schema_version; `ck_assessment_report_ready_requires_fields` requires non-null payload for report_ready), so the test seeded a valid object with a wrong-typed internal field plus a marker instead.
</p1>
<p2>
The Python lane delivered the three D handlers `assessment.analyze`, `identity.enroll`, `plan.generate` plus `handlers/dshared/` (constants with FIXED_NS, dconfig, providers with deterministic doubles + Aliyun adapters raising ProviderNotActivated, jsonschema_support, denqueue, dmedia, resolve) — 86 tests green. Decisions then: namespace-level enroll owner UUID `uuid5(FIXED_NS, "identity-namespace:{ns}")`, and a plan wait-hop bumping generation_revision + enqueuing a successor at MVP_PLAN_WAIT_CHECK_SECONDS=30 (both later reversed). A05's malformed-payload test deviated because V1 check constraints forbid a truncated/non-object report_payload.
</p2>
<p3>

<compartment start="49" end="54" title="plan.generate robustness fixes (revision cast, generating dead-end, step_id)" episode_type="bug" importance="52">
<p1>
I had the Python lane harden `plan_generate.py` on three bounded points. (1) `_SCAN_CAPABILITY` now regex-guards `revision` (`~ '^[0-9]+$'`) and uses a CASE-guarded cast with `ELSE -1`, so no `::int` is ever attempted on non-numeric/missing/structured revisions regardless of qualifier evaluation order. (2) The `status == 'generating'` + missing-baseline branch now calls `_transient_or_terminal(code="CAPABILITY_BASELINE_MISSING")` instead of `_wait_hop` — which was guarded on `waiting_inputs` and would no-op, letting the job succeed with no successor and strand the plan; non-final attempts requeue, and the attempt ceiling marks it failed with `failure_detail.code = CAPABILITY_BASELINE_MISSING`. (3) `_validate_candidate` now requires `step_id` to be a non-empty string ≤ 64 chars, else appends `$.steps[i].step_id: type violated` and never publishes. `d_support.py`'s `seed_microcrystal` type hint was widened from `int` to `Any` to seed malformed-revision rows. 93 tests green (7 new).
</p1>
<p2>
Three bounded `plan_generate.py` fixes: `_SCAN_CAPABILITY` regex-guards `revision` and uses a CASE-guarded cast (`ELSE -1`) so malformed revisions never hit `::int`; the `generating` + missing-baseline branch switches from the no-op `_wait_hop` to `CAPABILITY_BASELINE_MISSING` transient/terminal (so the plan can't be stranded); `_validate_candidate` requires `step_id` non-empty ≤64. 93 tests.
</p2>
<p3>
Hardened plan.generate against malformed capability revisions and a `generating` + missing-baseline dead-end, and added step_id validation.
</p3>
<p4>
plan_generate; CAPABILITY_BASELINE_MISSING; _SCAN_CAPABILITY cast guard
</p4>
</compartment>

<compartment start="55" end="58" title="Fixed reliable_new cross-cycle stall (D-E2E-1) + 总协调 six-item ruling" episode_type="bug" importance="78">
<p1>
I dispatched a fix for defect D-E2E-1: when `assessment.analyze` re-ran with a fresh process/double, the search still reported `reliable_new` even though our own prior enrollment had already created the member row, so the handler re-enqueued and raised `IDENTITY_ENROLLMENT_PENDING` forever. The fix computes `candidate_id = candidate_entity_id(ns, assessment_id)` and reconciles against PG: if a member exists, it sets `member_id` and `identity_result = {"schema_version":1,"classification":"reliable_new","phase":"enrolled_reconciled","candidate_entity_id":…,"member_id":…}` and falls through to the normal publish path; if absent it delegates to `_handle_reliable_new` exactly as before. The MATCHED-from-search path was untouched. 95 tests green, and I verified the new test genuinely covers the defect by temporarily forcing `reconciled_member_id = None` (the test failed as expected, then I restored the fix).

Then 总协调 sent a six-item incremental ruling on the coordination request and authoritative MD:

U: 媒体边界原则接受，术语改"授权可读集合"，不是公网公开；必须全量校验可信云台主体、当前指针、冻结报告引用及照片版本。

U: namespace级稳定UUID串行符合DD，保留确定性与未决登记阻塞，不改A helper。

U: 必须纠正 requiredViews：failure_detail 已确认仅内部诊断列，数据架构通用约束禁止用于业务决策或跨服务协议，不得从它投影 requiredViews。

U: 暂不接受等待方案：正常缺少能力不得每30秒generation_revision+1并创建succeeded后继任务。

U: media.cleanup 明确属于MVP，归D补齐最小handler及验证证据，不因D编号清单遗漏将其留作UNSUPPORTED_CONTRACT。

Item 1 accepted the media boundary but renamed the concept to "授权可读集合" (authorized-readable set), not public; item 2 kept the namespace-level deterministic UUID serialization and said not to change A's helper; item 3 forbade projecting requiredViews from `failure_detail` and required it to move into the existing versioned business JSON (identity_result); item 4 rejected the 30s wait-hop entirely — keep the same generation revision and logical task, use a lease-fenced deferral that doesn't consume a failed attempt, and don't rely on infinite successor jobs; item 5 assigned `media.cleanup` to D (minimal handler + verification evidence, idempotent, checking all T05/T01/T07/T13 references, no TTL on real data); item 6 accepted the remaining boundaries (initial generation revision, field-level updates, no K writes). I recorded the minimal coordination requests in `.mvp-d-runtime/coordination-request.md` for the Codex supervisor to sync.
</p1>
<p2>
Fixed defect D-E2E-1: `assessment.analyze` now reconciles `reliable_new` against PG — if a member row already exists for `candidate_entity_id(ns, assessment_id)` (our prior enrollment succeeded despite a fresh process reporting reliable_new), it reuses that `member_id`, sets `identity_result.phase="enrolled_reconciled"`, and publishes; member-absent behavior unchanged. 95 tests, with a forced-failure check proving the new test covers the defect.

总协调 then issued a six-item ruling:

U: 必须纠正 requiredViews：failure_detail 已确认仅内部诊断列，数据架构通用约束禁止用于业务决策或跨服务协议，不得从它投影 requiredViews。

U: 暂不接受等待方案：正常缺少能力不得每30秒generation_revision+1并创建succeeded后继任务。

U: media.cleanup 明确属于MVP，归D补齐最小handler及验证证据…

It kept the namespace-level deterministic UUID serialization (don't change A's helper), forbade the failure_detail→requiredViews projection (move it into identity_result), rejected the wait-hop in favor of a lease-fenced deferral that keeps the same generation revision/logical task and doesn't consume an attempt, and assigned `media.cleanup` to D.
</p2>
<p3>
Fixed the reliable_new cross-cycle stall by reconciling against PG for an already-enrolled member instead of re-enqueuing forever. 总协调 then ruled: requiredViews must not come from failure_detail (move to identity_result), capability waiting must not bump generation_revision or spawn successor jobs (use lease-fenced deferral), and media.cleanup belongs to D.
</p3>
<p4>
D-E2E-1; enrolled_reconciled; requiredViews off failure_detail; media.cleanup to D
</p4>
</compartment>

<compartment start="59" end="69" title="Rulings 3/5: Java off failure_detail + orphan media.cleanup enqueue" episode_type="bug,feature" importance="76">
<p1>
I had the Java lane implement rulings 3 and 5. For ruling 3, `AssessmentRepository.ViewRow` dropped `failureDetail` and added `identityResult` (findById selects `identity_result::text`, no longer `failure_detail`), and I removed the unused `failure_code`/`failure_detail` from `AcceptanceRow`/`findByIdForUpdate` too, so Java reads `failure_detail` nowhere (grep-verified; it is still cleared to NULL on retake, which is an allowed write). `FailureProjection` was rewritten: `requiredViews(status, identityResultJson)` reads `identity_result.quality.required_views` only when `status='needs_retake'`, filters to `[front,left,right]`, dedupes and caps at 3, malformed/missing → empty; `retryable(failureCode)` is a closed mapping (null → null, any non-null → false). `AssessmentReadService` wires both; `failureCode` is still emitted verbatim from `failure_code`.

For ruling 5, the new `MediaCleanupEnqueuer.enqueueOrphansFor(UUID t13RequestId)` selects `id FROM media_objects WHERE request_id=?
